scope: Original Fantasy Flight English 2008 CE01, 50 aliens; base rules and applicable official FAQ. Exclude Technology/variants, Anniversary extras and expansions.

required_facts: Deal two shuffled flares to each player; secretly choose one corresponding alien, return other sheet.
Include all six dealt flares plus four random extra flares: ten total.
Eight-card hands.
Draw destiny until a player color appears, that player starts; shuffle drawn card back into destiny.
One or more same-color ships on a planet are one colony.
Different colors can coexist, one colony per color per planet.
Five planets outside own system; may all be in same system.
source_references: Rulebook p2 What is a Colony/Game Overview

required_facts: Must retrieve one if available.
Any existing own home or foreign colony.
If no colonies, original rulebook places it directly in hyperspace gate.
Do not draw last card; shuffle with destiny discards then draw.
May redraw own color or attack one selected foreign colony in own system.
May reclaim completely ship-empty home planet with up to four ships from other colonies, a successful winning encounter through Launch only.
source_references: Rulebook p7 Destiny,p12 Driving Out Foreign Colonies
FAQ p3 reclaim counts as win,p4 through Launch

required_facts: No: Blue draw targets Blue in Blue home system.
Red defends own planet with zero ships.
Foreign colonies are bystanders: no defensive contribution, unaffected by outcome.
source_references: Rulebook p8 Can Macron Attack/Defending with Nothing/Bystanders

required_facts: One to four offense ships from any own colonies, same or several.
May strip but last ship removed immediately loses colony.
Defense cannot add or subtract ships on target.
source_references: Rulebook p8 Launch,p13 Stripping a Planet

required_facts: Offense invites then defense; invitees wait until both invitations.
Starting left of offense clockwise each accepts/declines and commits before next player.
One side only or neither; only invited side normally.
Each ally one to four ships from own colonies; defensive ships next to, not on target.
Totals16 each; defense wins ties.
Offense and offensive ally ships to warp.
Defense colony and bystanders remain.
Defensive allies return ships to any own colonies, no new colony on defended planet; receive one reward per committed ship.
source_references: Rulebook p9 Reveal,p11 If Defense Won

required_facts: Offense and offensive allies land on target, establish or reinforce colonies.
Defense and defensive allies to warp.
Bystanders survive.
Reinforcement of existing same-color colony is not new colony.
source_references: Rulebook p2 colony definition,p11 If Offense Won

required_facts: Three rewards, each one deck card or one own warp ship, may combine.
Allied ships return to any existing own colonies, even different origin.
Retrieved ships to any own colonies; no right to land on defended planet without existing colony.
Three random cards from opponent hand, not five; allied losses excluded.
Take entire hand if fewer than three.
Allies get no compensation.
Allies return to own colonies and get nothing, excluded from deal.
One minute; exchange hand cards and/or at most one colony per player on planet giver already occupies, own or foreign.
Use any recipient ships not in warp; coexist.
At least one card or colony changes hands, may be one-sided; promises unenforceable and tangible card terms must be honored.
Failure: each main player loses three chosen ships to warp; no second encounter.
Exact opponent encounter card initially revealed.
Later changes do not automatically alter Morph; it can be separately modified.
Returns to Morph identity after resolution and normally discarded with encounter cards.
Offense, defense or allies only.
Reveal after encounter cards revealed.
Either side, including opposing side.
Continue responses until all pass then resolve totals.
Player at most one flare per encounter; given flare once per encounter even transferred.
Immediately after effect resolves returns to hand.
Own matching alien must use Super normally; power lost or zapped allows only Wild until restored.
Cancellation targeting flare counts toward player limit.
Offense start: reveal/discard remaining hand, eight new cards.
Defense when required: reveal/discard, eight new, repeat until encounter card.
Other cards may legally be played beforehand but not compulsory.
Offense later when needs encounter card: turn ends, no new hand; gate offense and allies return to own colonies.
No automatic draw at encounter/turn end.
source_references: Rulebook p7 Starting Turn,p9 Planning,p13 Drawing New Cards

required_facts: No, need at least one encounter card in hand to start second.
First win or deal allows optional second; first loss or failed deal ends turn.
After second ends regardless outcome, pass left.
source_references: Rulebook p7 The Turn,p11 After Resolving

required_facts: Fewer than three home colonies: immediately lose, turn sheet down; no last use.
Regain at least three home colonies: restore faceup.
Zap cancels use and further uses current encounter; clauses not requiring use still function, e.g. Warrior experience and Zombie deal liberation.
source_references: Rulebook p12 Losing Alien Powers/Zapping Powers

required_facts: Offense, defense, other players clockwise from left of offense.
Complete effect before another except Zap or specific interruption permission.
No preemptive Cosmic Zap; must power use.
Ordinary win checked at very end of Resolution; opportunity to stop it until then.
Simultaneous five foreign colonies share win.
Tick-Tock last token on successful deal shares three-way win with both main players.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Planning.
After encounter cards are selected but before reveal, if you have at least one ship in encounter, may increase or decrease your ships there.
May remove some or all of your ships to your colonies, or add any number (even above normal maximum four) from any of your colonies.
If you win but have no ships left in the encounter, cannot receive a colony.
Role: Main player only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Reveal.
After both main players reveal attack cards, use power to make lower total win.
When used, your ships and any offensive and defensive allies' ships are subtracted from the appropriate side's card.
Opponent's total is otherwise figured normally.
Defense still wins ties under the unchanged general tie rule.
Role: Offense only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Resolution.
After winning an encounter, before compensation (if any) collected, use power to loot opponent's cards.
Take and look at opponent's hand. For each of your ships in encounter, may choose one card from that hand and add it to own.
Afterwards discard remainder of opponent's hand.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Planning.
After cards selected but before reveal, may declare an equalize.
If both revealed cards are attack cards, higher card's value is reduced by lower card's value; lower card retains its value.
Printed example: 15 versus 8 becomes 7 versus 8. Conclude encounter normally.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Reveal.
After revealing encounter cards, may pray for divine intervention once per encounter: draw three cards from deck.
If none are encounter cards discard them, no further effect. If any are encounter cards may choose one to replace own revealed encounter card (discard replaced card).
If own revealed card and chosen replacement are both attacks, may instead add chosen card value to revealed attack value, or replace as normal.
Discard all other drawn cards; resolve encounter with new card or card value.
Role: As any player; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Planning.
During each player's turn after destiny drawn, may play an attack card from hand faceup next to any planet in any system as a citadel.
If planet with one or more citadels attacked, after encounter cards selected but before reveal may use power to activate ALL citadels on that planet.
Add combined value of activated citadels to defense total.
If activated and defense loses, discard citadels. If defense wins or citadels not activated, they stay.
Placing a citadel does not require power use; activating the citadels does.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Resolution.
After encounter resolved and any compensation claimed, may use power to return own encounter card to hand instead of discarding.
Role: Main player only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Resolution.

When you win an encounter in which you revealed an attack card, use power to force opponent to lose extra ships of opponent's choice equal to number of your ships in encounter, in addition to normal losses.
A deal is a successful encounter.
A deal is not a win for effects such as Cudgel or Barbarian that do not explicitly include deals.
No; the originally revealed card controls the revealed-attack trigger, so Cudgel cannot use its power on that basis.
Role: Not offense; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Destiny.
When not offense, before destiny chosen, use power to take destiny deck, look through it and choose any card; played as though offense had drawn it.
On own turn, or any time zapped, remaining destiny cards shuffled and one dealt randomly.
Role: As any player; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Resolution.
After encounter cards discarded at end of encounter, may retrieve one of those discarded cards and offer to another player.
If refused, may keep it. If accepted, other player keeps it, then you may either retrieve one ship from warp or draw one card from deck.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Resolution.
After encounter cards discarded at end of encounter, may retrieve opponent's card from discard pile and add to own hand.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Reveal.

After both main players reveal attack cards, may discard any or all attack cards in hand that are BOTH higher than own played attack and lower than opponent's played attack; add their values to own total.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Reveal.
After opponent reveals encounter card may keep own facedown, stating what it is; may lie.
If opponent does not challenge, conclude encounter as if statement true; place own encounter card facedown on bottom of deck instead of discarding.
If challenged reveal own card. If you lied, lose as many ships to warp as you had in encounter. If truth, opponent loses as many ships as opponent had in encounter.
Those lost ships MAY NOT be ships involved in encounter. Afterwards conclude normally using revealed cards.
Do not use with Sorcerer.
Role: Main player only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Alliance.
After alliances formed, give grudge token to each player invited by you who did not ally with you.
If you win or make deal, each grudge-token player discards it and loses one ship of their choice to warp.
If you lose or fail deal, each grudge-token player discards it and loses four ships of their choice to warp.
Lost ships cannot include ships used to ally with the other side.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Resolution.
When collecting compensation may choose player to collect from, whether or not opponent. Look through that player's hand and choose desired compensation cards.
When opponent collects compensation from you, may select cards opponent gets.
Role: Offense only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Start Turn.
At start of own turn use power; first choose and discard a card from hand.
Every other player must choose either discard same card type (attack, negotiate, artifact, etc.) or lose three ships of YOUR choice to warp.
If discarded card attack, opponents must discard attack of equal or higher value. Opponent with no cards of discarded type must lose ships instead.
If after using power you have no encounter cards in hand, draw new hand.
Role: As any player; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal, Resolution.
When ANOTHER player loses ships to warp or has ships removed from game, may return ALL ships just lost to that player and earn one deck card.
Healing does not prevent compensation. Healed player replaces ships on any of their colonies.
During encounter may heal several players, drawing one card for each.
Role: Main player or ally only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Reveal.
After encounter cards revealed use power to add 4 to own side's total.
If power zapped, own side automatically wins encounter.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Planning.
Before encounter cards selected may send up to four own ships from any own colonies to warp. Draw two deck cards for every ship sent.
If power zapped, sacrificed ships are not lost to warp.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Planning.
Before encounter cards selected may declare upset. Once declared both main players must play attack cards if possible.
After reveal winning side loses and losing side wins.
Occurs after ALL other game effects resolved, including Human's power being zapped.
Role: Offense only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Resolution.
Own turn is not limited to two encounters.
After completing an encounter, successful or not, may have another encounter as long as at least one encounter card remains in own hand.
Role: Main player or ally only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Launch, Alliance, Reveal.
As offense use before launching ships. As ally use after allies invited. As main player or ally, use after reveal for ship strength.
As offense or ally may send only ONE ship into encounter.
Each own ship adds 4 instead of 1 to own side's total.
When collecting compensation or rewards, each own ship worth TWO ships.
Defense does not have the one-ship launch restriction.
Each Macron ship counts as one ship for a number-of-ships condition, not four.
source_references: Official FAQ May6 2009 p1 Macron erratum; 2018 FAQp17

required_facts: Role: As any player; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Regroup.
At start of any player's regroup phase, BEFORE offense retrieves warp ship, use power to win if all your ships lost.
Lost ships include those in warp, removed from game, and captured by other players.
Do not lose power for too few home colonies. May still win normally.
An explicitly immediate winning effect ends the game when it resolves, without waiting for the end of Resolution.
A Zap or an effect specifically permitting interruption can interrupt it.
Role: As any player; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Alliance.
Before allies invited may look at entire hand of ONE main player. If main player, may look at opponent's hand.
May NOT tell any other players what cards seen in a player's hand using power.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Planning.
After encounter cards selected but before revealed may call reversal.
Reverse digits of any attack cards revealed in this encounter; resolve encounter using reversed values.
Examples: 15 becomes 51, 20 becomes 02, 08 becomes 80.
Role: As any player; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal, Resolution.
Deal TWO separate eight-card hands; look at them and choose one hoard, facedown on sheet.
Whenever wishing to play a card, may use power to play from hoard instead of normal hand.
May not add gained cards to hoard; other players may not look at or draw cards from hoard.
If hoard has no encounter cards, may reveal it, discard it, and get new eight-card hoard.
Role: Offense only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Launch.
Before allies invited, if defense has more than three cards, use power. Defense must either discard down to THREE cards at random or let you establish colony on targeted world.
If granted colony, land any own ships in gate on targeted planet; coexist with defense ships (which do not go to warp); encounter immediately ends successfully.
If defense discards down to three at random, continue normally.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Alliance.
Before allies invited, if fewer than eight cards, may refill hand.
Draw cards ONE AT A TIME, at random, from any player(s) or deck until full hand of eight.
Role: Main player or ally only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Resolution.
As ally, whenever own ships should be lost to warp, instead return to any own colonies and keep using them.
As main player, whenever any own allies should lose ships to warp, instead allow those allies to return ships to any of their colonies of their choice.
Role: Main player only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Planning.
Before encounter cards selected, force opponent to play encounter card FACEUP.
Only after seeing opponent's card select and play own card.
Role: Main player only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Reveal.
If you reveal negotiate and opponent attack, use power to win encounter.
If both reveal negotiate, attempt deal as usual.
Role: Not main player; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Alliance.
When own turn to ally, may ally with either side as if invited even when not invited, sending one to four ships as usual.
Cannot bypass another game effect specifically preventing alliance, e.g. Force Field artifact.
Role: Main player or ally only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Alliance.
After alliances formed may give ONE hand card to either main player; if main player must give to opponent.
Recipient immediately adds card to hand and may play it normally.
If afterwards own hand has no encounter cards AND you are main player, draw new hand.
Role: Main player or ally only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Resolution.
When losing encounter or failing deal, draw alien power at random from unused pile and become that alien.
Redraw if alien has Game Setup text or is not allowed in current game.
If lose later encounter, discard that alien and draw new one. Retain Reincarnator power while using others.
Aliens able to copy power may copy BOTH Reincarnator and currently reincarnated power; if they lose an encounter while copying must reincarnate, losing original power.
Role: As any player; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal, Resolution.
Whenever another player retrieves one or more warp ships, may retrieve ONE own warp ship as well.
May NOT retrieve ship in same encounter it went to warp.
Whenever another player draws one or more deck cards, may draw ONE deck card as well.
Role: Main player or ally only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Reveal.
After encounter cards revealed may play one or more attack cards of 06 OR LESS from hand as reinforcement cards of listed value.
When another player plays reinforcement, may use power and discard negotiate card to cancel and discard that reinforcement.
Role: As any player; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Destiny.
Whenever any OTHER player's color or special destiny targeting another player drawn, choose one of that player's ships from any colony of YOUR choice and send to warp.
On wild destiny may execute one ship of ANY other player regardless of whom offense chooses to attack.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Planning.
After encounter cards selected but before reveal may switch encounter cards with opponent; opponent reveals your card and you reveal opponent's.
Gambler sheet says do not use Gambler with Sorcerer.
Role: Offense only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Resolution.
When losing encounter, if both main players revealed attacks AND you lost by 10 OR MORE, including low-total-wins encounters, may land ONE own ship otherwise lost to warp on winning defensive planet.
Ship coexists with ships already there.
Does not allow coexistence in places or with aliens that state otherwise.
source_references: Official FAQ May6 2009 p1 Spiff erratum

required_facts: Role: As any player; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Resolution.
Place ten tokens on sheet.
Each time any player wins as defense OR successful deal made between any two players, discard one token from sheet.
If no tokens left on sheet immediately win game. May also win normally.
Role: Main player only; use: Optional.
Phase(s): Planning.
Before encounter cards selected may trade hands with opponent. Both then keep new hands.
Role: Main player only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Reveal.
After revealing attack, adjust its value: 10 OR LESS triple value; MORE THAN 10 divide value by three, rounded up.
Attack10→30; attack11→4.
Role: As any player; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal, Resolution.
Whenever own ships lost to warp, take along UP TO equal number of other ships.
YOU specify affected players and how many ships each must lose. Targeted players choose colony/colonies ships come from.
Losses to Vacuum in addition to normal encounter losses.
Cannot target itself.
Role: Main player only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Reveal.
After revealing attack, multiply number of OWN ships in encounter by own attack-card value instead of adding.
Allies' ships still added to total as usual.
Role: Main player only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Resolution.
When winning encounter remove LOSING SIDE'S ships from game instead of sending to warp.
Cannot reduce any player to fewer ships than number of foreign colonies needed to win game.
Eradicated ships that would reduce player below this number go to warp normally.
Standard minimum is five ships remaining in game, counting ships in warp as still in game; from six ships with three losses, eradicate one and send two to warp.
Role: As any player; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal, Resolution.
Whenever any OTHER player discards artifact, whether after playing or not, add artifact to own hand.
Own played artifacts discarded normally and CANNOT be salvaged.
When drawing new hand, retain old artifacts AFTER revealing them, then draw eight new cards IN ADDITION.
Role: Main player only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Reveal.
After revealing attack add 1 to own total for EACH ship in warp, yours or otherwise.
Role: Main player only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Reveal.
After an encounter as MAIN PLAYER, add one token for win/deal or two for loss/faileddeal.
As main player after revealing attack use power to add 1 to own total per sheet token; tokens NOT discarded.
Yes; its experience-earning clause still functions because it does not require power use.
source_references: Official FAQ May6 2009 p1 Warrior erratum; FAQ2018p22

required_facts: Role: Offense only; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Destiny.
After drawing destiny use power to encounter ANY alien on ANY planet of own choice instead of alien mandated by destiny.
Example: may encounter Virus ships on Mind planet although destiny directed Oracle.
Any OTHER effects caused by drawn destiny still occur normally.
When targeting a third-player system, the chosen defense must have a colony there; home owner can defend its empty planet.
Role: As any player; use: Mandatory.
Phase(s): Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal, Resolution.
Whenever own ships should be lost to warp, instead return them to any own colonies and keep using them.
Deal liberation is a non-use clause; may liberate any number of negotiating opponent's ships, not a third player's, back to that opponent's colonies.
Cosmic Quake: all players discard all cards, shuffle the discard pile into a new cosmic deck, and deal eight cards to every player.
If insufficient, discard and reshuffle all cosmic cards, including Miser's hoard; replenish setup card holdings such as the hoard as at game setup.
Ordinary Zombie prevention and Void eradication earn no compensation because the ships never reach the warp.
Zapped Zombie can receive compensation for its ships actually lost to the warp.
contextual_background: The main player revealed a negotiate against an attack; the question concerns otherwise qualifying compensation.

required_facts: Losing ships are involved main-player/allied ships that should go to the warp because of the encounter.
Lost ships actually go to the warp involuntarily; sent ships go because of a specific action/effect, sometimes voluntarily, are not directly involved in the encounter, and count as lost.
A losing Zombie ship can be prevented from going to the warp and therefore is not lost.
Legal cards may be played in their ordinary timing windows before compensation begins.
Once Hacker targets the hand, the earlier reinforcement opportunity has passed; ordinary card play cannot interrupt the hand-targeting effect.
Only a Zap or a power/effect explicitly permitting interruption can interrupt it.
contextual_background: The reinforcement can be played only while its normal timing window is open; no permission to play it during compensation is assumed.

required_facts: Released ships with no colony to return to are returned to the warp.
The offense may first place up to four of its released ships in the hyperspace gate.
Start Turn occurs only on the first offensive encounter of a turn.
Start Turn effects happen before Regroup effects; the offense draws its required new hand before a Regroup Plague can be played.
Discard non-encounter cards first in alphabetical and numerical order.
Then discard encounter cards beginning with offense and proceeding clockwise, ending with defense; the defense's encounter card is on top.
Proceed only through Launch.
The reclamation is both a win and a successful encounter.
Warrior earns experience for that win.
May place up to four ships.
Ships come from the player's other existing colonies; this rule does not permit direct retrieval from the warp.
source_references: Original rulebook p7 extraction lines549–553; p12 lines974–979

required_facts: An involved ship cannot pay an explicitly outside-encounter sacrifice cost.
A forced loss of outside ships loses nothing if no outside ships exist.
Proceed with the encounter even with no offensive ships.
Winning with no ships does not establish a foreign colony unless an effect explicitly allows it.
A player may make false claims about hand contents.
Cards cannot be shown to others absent an effect requiring/allowing it.
Hand size must be disclosed on request.
Table talk must be public.
contextual_background: No applicable alien or card creates a secrecy, disclosure or private-communication exception.

required_facts: Encounter totals use the modified current value/type.
Unrelated identity-targeting effects use the original printed identity/type/value.
Morph remains a Morph by original identity, while counting as the copied attack for encounter totals.
These effects strictly affecting encounter resolution also use the card's current modified type/value, unless a specific effect says otherwise.
Discard piles are public unless a rule/effect specifies otherwise.
Every simultaneously discarded faceup card may be inspected unless a power says otherwise.
No; after losing the power the player is not considered that alien.
For Fodder and Reserve, choose the cards for the power together rather than resolving repeated incremental selections.
Kamikaze must sacrifice all chosen ships at once before drawing any cards.
Yes; defensive allies are considered in the hyperspace gate for such effects.
The player losing the extra ships chooses them unless the effect specifies otherwise.
A forced loss, sacrifice or transfer normally chooses a ship under that player's control, subject to the effect's restrictions.
contextual_background: Optional researching-Tech examples are excluded; any location restriction printed on the effect still applies.

required_facts: The six base types are attack, negotiate, morph, artifact, flare and reinforcement.
Morph is its own type and a held Morph must be discarded for its type.
Encounter is not a separate card type.
Remove the alien bearing the printed restriction; retain the one without it.
The affected player may use its previously rejected alien or draw a replacement flare and become that alien.
Redraw if the replacement produces another conflict.
No; a legal encounter must permit offense ultimately to gain a foreign colony without necessarily making a deal.
There is no universal one-use-per-encounter limit: a power is usable once per relevant context unless its text says otherwise.
Hate specifies once per turn.
Vulch can act whenever another player discards a qualifying artifact.
Yes; the player may change that decision when another action/timing outcome changes the state.
The giver does not vacate; the colonies coexist unless an effect specifies otherwise.
A deal may be one-sided if at least one card or colony changes hands.
Future promises may be included but are unenforceable.
Explicit card/colony terms cannot be lied about and must be fulfilled.
A cancellation targeting the flare itself counts against the player's one-flare allowance.
An Anti-Matter-prevented flare stays in hand and does not count against that allowance.
The prevented flare may not be attempted again in the same encounter.
contextual_background: Only cancellation of the flare itself is assumed; the card destination after Card Zap is not asked or scored here.

required_facts: Keep the flare after resolving its effect.
contextual_background: The question supplies the flare's transfer/discard clause as background; no unquoted flare identity or effect is scored.

required_facts: Yes; Cosmic Zap can cancel the actual power use enabled by the Super, including the altered role and altered phase.
Neither discard nor immediate Wild play is required; the flare remains in hand.
While the power is zapped only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play.
Canceling the enabled power does not cancel or undo the already-played flare; ordinary per-player and per-flare once-per-encounter limits still prevent a second play absent an explicit exception.
source_references: Original rulebook p13 Flare Cards; 2018 FAQ p6 extraction lines525–537

required_facts: The immediate effect can be observed before deciding to Zap within the short same-phase opportunity.
Once later action such as reinforcement play has passed that window, the earlier use cannot be retroactively zapped.
Moving into the next phase closes the opportunity.
No; Start Turn is part of the same encounter, so the power remains zapped through that encounter.
All twenty chosen ships move as one complete effect.
Amoeba loses its power after the move has completed, not partway through it.
contextual_background: Amoeba began with its power active and this is a legal invocation; ordinary ooze eligibility is background, not scored.

required_facts: It still counts as having allied.
It receives no Grudge token for failing to ally, provided it initially committed at least one ship.
Yes; a zero-ship defense can use the flare to increase the ship count.
Each listed flare must be played in each encounter in which its effect is desired; none becomes an automatic persistent effect for later encounters merely from one play.
After inspecting the cards.
The citadels remain when the sheet is turned facedown.
The citadels are discarded when the sheet is discarded.
Clone keeps the card that ends in front of Clone.
Filch takes the card that ends in front of its opponent.
Clone takes precedence and keeps its card.
Filch versus Fido uses the ordinary timing rules.
Clone may choose an amount between normal compensation and double normal compensation.
The opponent must have sufficient cards for the chosen amount.
source_references: Original rulebook p5 printed Clone Super illustration

required_facts: No; Mind cannot inspect Miser's hoard.
Fido must choose from encounter cards actually played in the encounter.
It cannot choose cards merely discarded to Plague, Fodder or Reserve.
Filch cannot take it.
The unrevealed card is placed on the bottom of the cosmic deck rather than discarded.
No; Fodder Wild permits joining only a side that originally invited the player that encounter.
They must be lower than the opponent's card, regardless of Fodder's own card.
The flare does not permit discarding attacks above the opponent's card.
Gambler must reveal its card or bluff before Oracle chooses its encounter card.
Hate may discard Morph; each other player must discard Morph or lose ships.
A player cannot discard an insufficient lower attack; if it does not discard a qualifying attack it discards nothing and loses three ships.
Offensive Hate draws a necessary new hand before using its power.
If zapped after selecting its discard, Hate keeps that card.
Healer returns ships after they have entered the warp; this can trigger Remora.
Healer cannot heal Zombie ships that are prevented from reaching the warp.
Vacuum has already lost ships to the warp and can use its power before healing.
Healer may then heal other eligible affected ships, but not its own ships.
Use the ordinary timing order; whichever of those conflicting effects goes off first wins.
Human can be zapped to win even if one or both revealed cards are negotiates.
The opposing negotiate receives compensation only if Human actually revealed an attack.
Yes; Cosmic Zap can target its own player's power use.
source_references: Original rulebook p5 printed Cosmic Zap illustration

required_facts: Yes; it may add eight, then choose to discard the flare for the zap.
It may also forego adding eight and discard solely for the zap effect.
Play Machine Wild faceup outside the hand.
Discard the old hand and draw a new eight-card hand if needed for the guaranteed second encounter.
Return the Machine flare to hand after its effect resolves.
At launch, a Zap permits launching up to four ships worth one each.
After reveal, a Zap removes Macron's four-per-ship value.
Macron Super permits up to four ships as a defensive ally too.
One play of each listed flare lasts through the current encounter, allowing the eligible later triggering events without replay.
Vulch Super is played the first time eligible flares are discarded in that encounter.
Vulch cannot retrieve its own Super by that effect.
Whenever another player discards a reinforcement card during the remaining encounter, Reserve Wild's user may take it.
Add the taken reinforcement to the user's own hand; this does not grant retrieval of the user's own reinforcement discards.
A card played from the hoard returns to the hoard, including flares.
An encounter card only in the hoard does not permit a second encounter.
Miser can satisfy required hand discards from the hoard, including Hate.
Yes; saving fewer than two is allowed.
Observer protects all its ships as an ally, including outside-encounter Grudge losses; protected ships may instead be relocated as described.
Observer can use Void Wild without paying the ship loss while its protection applies.
The protection applies only during Resolution, not earlier phases.
Pacifist receives compensation if Loser revealed an attack.
It receives no compensation otherwise.
No; defense must play the given card.
Yes; associated cards/holdings such as Miser's hoard go with the lent power.
The flare takes effect after the end of the encounter, so earlier same-phase power use is allowed.
Reincarnator Wild cannot target its own player; it specifies another player.
Reincarnator cannot use the Super flares of its incarnations.
Reserve keeps the card because the Zap prevents it from being played.
Shadow executes once for each card drawn.
Trader cannot trade an empty hand; it must first draw a new hand, then may use its power to trade.
Vacuum cannot target itself.
The losses from one Vacuum Super effect are simultaneous.
Zombie cannot redirect a saved ship into another colony being removed in that same effect; the affected colonies can all be lost.
Yes; without allies it multiplies by zero.
Failed-deal losses are not eradicated.
Void eradicates on a win as main player, or as ally when using its Super.
Void trumps both Zombie and Observer because the ships are eradicated without going to the warp.
Vulch cannot retrieve the Zap that zapped it because its power is unavailable when that Zap is discarded.
An active Vulch can retrieve artifacts discarded by the Vulch Wild holder and may then have to return them again.
Ships arriving before Warpish's power use count in that use.
Ships arriving afterward do not update that already-used power's total; use timing rules when needed.
Yes; it may invoke the card and use its power to prevent those ships from reaching the warp.
Retrieve one ship from the warp.
The retrieved ship may be placed on any of that player's home planets.
contextual_background: This asks only the FAQ's named no-colonies/no-ships-on-own-turn case; it does not generalize home-planet recovery to every no-colony situation.

required_facts: Hacker's compensation resolves first because offense precedes the other player in the timing order.
contextual_background: The scenario gives Hacker's eligible compensation target and the ally's pending rewards; the printed power's target-selection mechanism is not scored here.
Required fact is a direct application of FAQ timing order, rather than a newly asserted Hacker-specific priority.

required_facts: Removing last ship immediately eliminates colony.
Ordinary returning/retrieved ships cannot use that abandoned location as an existing colony.
Required relocation with no colony goes to warp unless a specific exception applies.
source_references: Rulebook p13 Stripping a Planet of Ships

required_facts: Original rulebook permits driving out a foreign colony after a self-designating special, as after own color.
Offense chooses one player's foreign colony as defense in own system.
All other colonies are bystanders and unaffected.
contextual_background: This conditional is explicitly stated in the original core rulebook; it does not posit an expansion effect.
source_references: Rulebook p12 Driving Out Foreign Colonies

required_facts: Oracle acts before selecting its card, forcing Sorcerer to play faceup.
Oracle sees that card, then selects and plays its own facedown.
Only after both selections may Sorcerer switch encounter cards, before revealing Oracle's card.
The before/after-selection timings govern; not simultaneous merely because both are Planning.
source_references: Printed original Oracle and Sorcerer sheets

required_facts: May retain the artifact instead of discarding it.
Printed permission is to play it again during a later encounter, not repeated replay in the same encounter.
Any player; any phase, with artifact's own legal timing still relevant.
source_references: Rulebook p5 printed Clone flare illustration, Wild text and role/phase

required_facts: May illicitly take own ships from warp to colonies or cards from deck/discard even without entitlement.
Does not need reveal unless caught, then may be zapped.
If caught lose one ship to warp and return items caught filching.
Once revealed deck/discards placed next to user for access.
contextual_background: Only one of standard and classic Filch flare is used; any-phase/as-any-player printed usage.
source_references: Rulebook p5 printed classic Filch Wild illustration

required_facts: As any player during Reveal.
May filch any other player's used encounter card whether involved or not.
source_references: Original rulebook p5 printed classic Filch Super illustration

required_facts: Play when another player draws a card from the cosmic deck.
For rest of encounter intercept cards that same player must draw, not every player's later draws.
User draws, inspects, and gives each card to that player.
May not share the information with other players.
source_references: Official May6 2009 FAQ p1 Mind Flare erratum, cached extraction L43–49

required_facts: After another player besides Reincarnator loses or fails a deal, may give them the flare.
Immediately after end of encounter target discards current power and draws a new one.
Reject Game Setup and disallowed aliens and draw again.
source_references: Official May6 2009 FAQ p1 Reincarnator Flare erratum, cached extraction L50–58

required_facts: Warp in center; each player chooses a color and takes its five planets.
Each player has twenty ships, four on each home planet.
Colony markers begin beside the warp at zero foreign colonies.
Remove destiny cards for unused player colors; retain used colors, wilds and specials and shuffle.
Use either standard or classic Filch flare, only one version; return the other to box.
source_references: Original rulebook p6 Setup steps1–3,5; p5 Alternate Filch

required_facts: Wild permits choosing another player, encountered in that player's home system.
Special states defense conditions and location; follow its text.
For effects special is treated as the designated defense's color.
Hazard symbols have no effect in this original base game.
Neither main player may invite the other.
Non-main players normally need invitation; may decline all invitations.
Each ally commits one to four own ships from any own colonies.
Only offense and defense select one encounter card each: attack, negotiate or Morph.
Normally placed facedown at Planning and revealed simultaneously at Reveal, subject to powers.
Normally discard revealed encounter cards after resolving encounter, unless an effect changes destination.
source_references: Original rulebook p9 Alliance/Planning/Reveal,p11 After Resolving Encounter

required_facts: Artifacts cannot be played as encounter cards.
Each artifact's printed timing and instructions determine when/how it can be played.
Normally discard an artifact after playing it.
Any of the recipient's own ships not in the warp may establish its deal colony; not restricted to gate ships.
Any offensive ships remaining on gate after the deal return to any of offense's existing colonies.
source_references: Original rulebook p10 If Both Players Reveal Negotiate Cards

required_facts: Must declare all reward sources before taking any rewards, including the complete base cosmic-card/warp-ship mix.
Cannot inspect an initial draw before deciding remaining reward sources.
contextual_background: The reward-deck components in the source example remain excluded; only its general all-sources commitment rule is tested.
source_references: Official FAQ through2018 p8, Reward Deck, extractionlines759–765; independently identified source auditPSA-001

required_facts: The ships land on colonies simultaneously.
contextual_background: No Saboteur trap, token or revelation commitment rule is imported.
source_references: 2018 FAQ p19 extraction lines1796–1797: general simultaneous-landing statement explicitly illustrated by base Mobius Tubes.

required_facts: No automatic draw is caused merely by an encounter ending, a turn ending or the hand becoming empty.
The offense points the gate at one planet in the system indicated by destiny.
Place the launched offense ships on the wide end of the hyperspace gate.
Place the joining offensive ally's ships on the hyperspace gate.
Receive one defender reward for each ship contributed to the successful defense.
For each contributed ship the ally must draw one cosmic-deck card or retrieve one own warp ship; the ordinary rule does not permit declining the reward.
contextual_background: Mixing the two sources and reward destinations are already asked by Q010; full-source commitment before taking any is Q155.

required_facts: Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal, Resolution, in that order.
Start Turn occurs before the first encounter's Regroup effects, and only on that first encounter.
contextual_background: Only the complete seven-phase order adds novelty; Start Turn versus Regroup was already asked by Q076.

required_facts: Add the legally played reinforcement card's printed amount to the chosen side's encounter total.
contextual_background: The attack-versus-attack case avoids choosing an interpretation of the pending reinforcement/Negotiate conflict.
